hints.title: Threshold Partition Strategy
hints.text: Sort the array. There is an optimal index i such that elements up to i increase by k while remaining elements decrease by k.

hints.title: Extreme Values After Shift
hints.text: For partition point i, the candidate maximum is max(nums[i] + k, nums[-1] - k) and candidate minimum is min(nums[0] + k, nums[i+1] - k).

hints.title: Minimum Spread Tracking
hints.text: Iterate i across 0 to n - 2, updating the global minimum difference between candidate maximum and minimum.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def smallestRangeII(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        nums.sort()
        ans = nums[-1] - nums[0]
        for i in range(len(nums) - 1):
            hi = max(nums[-1] - k, nums[i] + k)
            lo = min(nums[0] + k, nums[i + 1] - k)
            ans = min(ans, hi - lo)
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Sorting followed by linear partition boundary scan.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all 2^N combinations of +k and -k choices causes exponential blowup.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant auxiliary space when sorted in place.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Prove that only monotonic prefixes get +k and suffixes get -k in the sorted array.
